scope: Desktop/browser screen-share profile consistency and live reconfiguration across guild LiveKit, group LiveKit and P2P calls
implementation: Shared codec, bitrate and degradation policy; detail mode preserves resolution priority even with low latency enabled
Distinct H264 lower layers, at most two, with bounded lower-layer frame rates
LiveKit retains the captured source and republishes only video for codec/encoding changes; profile-only changes apply in place
LiveKit transitions serialize, restore the prior publication on failure, retain SDK negotiated options, and retire pending sources on stop/admission loss
Guild initial starts/stops serialize; cancelled picker results cannot stop a newer share; screen audio stops even during a video publication gap
P2P codec preference changes use existing serialized negotiation with exact offer acknowledgement, capability checks, reported fallback detection and camera policy restoration
Private/group controls expose low-latency and content-profile preferences

targeted_regressions.command: npx vitest run src/webrtc src/stores/p2pCallStore src/components/dm/GroupScreenShare src/hooks/useScreenShareToggle.test.tsx src/utils/privateScreenQuality.test.ts src/utils/screenShareProfile.test.ts src/hooks/useEncryptedRoomAdmission.test.tsx

limits: Tests use simulated capture/signaling with real SDK track wrappers where applicable; they do not establish production browser/peer interoperability
Hardware encoding, capture-to-display latency, packet-loss recovery, actual quality and long-duration calls have not been measured
Codec/encoding republishing can briefly interrupt received video; zero-gap switching is not claimed
P2P preference acknowledgement does not prove hardware encoding; absent/stale codec stats remain unknown
Native Capacitor screen-sharing bridge is outside this change
No deployment or production settings changes were performed
